subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared multi-encoding filename decoder live, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/71517 be refreshed or replaced?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent boundary affects media-core exports, bundled channel plugins, and plugin-facing reuse; automation should not choose that API direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use a media-core or SDK-safe helper
options.body: Put the decoder behind a plugin-safe media-core/exported boundary and refresh or replace the open PR around that single helper.

options.title: Keep only narrow channel fixes
options.body: Treat current Feishu repairs as enough for now and defer non-Feishu multi-encoding cases until concrete reports arrive.

options.title: Require broader live repros first
options.body: Keep this issue open but ask for real non-Feishu channel failures before approving the shared utility surface.

recommendation.title: Use a media-core or SDK-safe helper
recommendation.body: Put the decoder behind a plugin-safe media-core/exported boundary and refresh or replace the open PR around that single helper.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Feishu filename repair and release/media-core context make this the strongest available owner for the boundary decision.
